content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-physics-average-speed","title":"Average Speed","quick":"Average speed = total distance divided by total time. It tells how fast something moves overall, not at every single moment.","full":"Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time. Example: an auto goes to the market 120 km away and takes 2 hours. Average speed = 120/2 = 60 km/h. This does not mean it went exactly 60 km/h every minute - it may have gone faster on open road, slower near traffic - 60 km/h is the overall rate. Always keep units matching: km with hours gives km/h.","traps":["Forgetting to divide and just writing the distance or time as the answer","Mixing units, like using minutes with km without converting","Writing the answer without correct unit (km/h)"],"misconception":"Child thinks average speed means the speed stayed exactly the same the whole journey.","parent_questions":[{"q":"What formula do we use to find average speed?","expected_answer_hint":"Average speed = Total distance / Total time"},{"q":"If the car does not go the same speed whole way, can we still find one average speed?","expected_answer_hint":"Yes, average speed is one overall value even if speed changes during the trip"}],"check_question":{"q":"A bus travels 90 km in 3 hours.
